metadata.summary: This guideline addresses the epidemiology, risk factors, pathology, diagnosis, staging and prognosis of upper urinary tract urothelial carcinoma. It covers risk-adapted management of localised and metastatic disease, including kidney-sparing procedures, radical surgery, systemic treatment and follow-up. Its recommendations are intended to support individual clinical decisions alongside patient circumstances and preferences.

toxicities.incidence: In a single-arm phase III trial of 71 patients, ureteric stenosis occurred in 31 (44%); 19/31 (61%) of those with stenosis required treatment.
In a single-arm phase III trial of 71 patients, urinary tract infection occurred in 23 (32%).
In a single-arm phase III trial of 71 patients, haematuria occurred in 22 (31%).
In a single-arm phase III trial of 71 patients, flank pain occurred in 21 (30%).
In a single-arm phase III trial of 71 patients, nausea occurred in 17 (24%).
In the EV302 study, skin reactions were reported among grade 3 or above treatment-related adverse events of special interest in 15.5% of patients receiving the combination.
In the EV302 study, peripheral neuropathy was reported among grade 3 or above treatment-related adverse events of special interest in 6.8% of patients receiving the combination.
In the EV302 study, hyperglycaemia was reported among grade 3 or above treatment-related adverse events of special interest in 6.1% of patients receiving the combination.
In the adjuvant phase III trial, treatment-related adverse events > grade 3 occurred in 17.9% of the nivolumab group and 7.2% of the placebo group.
A neoadjuvant phase II study involving 10 patients with high-risk UTUC reported one treatment-related death.
A review of renal function after RNU reported GFR levels of around 50 mls/min at three months.
prevention: The guide identifies the ability to administer cisplatin-based NAC while renal function remains maximal as an advantage of treatment before RNU.
During RNU, avoid opening the urinary tract except for bladder cuff excision after clipping the ureter and fully draining the bladder.
Keep instruments from directly contacting the tumour, use a closed operative system, avoid tumour morcellation and extract the tumour in an endobag.

Remove the kidney, ureter and bladder cuff together. An open approach is favoured for large or invasive tumours (T3/T4 and/or N+/M+) because oncological outcomes may be better than with minimally-invasive RNU.

prophylaxis.recommendation: Administer one post-operative intravesical chemotherapy instillation to reduce bladder recurrence after RNU. The evidence discussed concerns mitomycin C or pirarubicin; if drug extravasation is a concern, a cystogram may be considered before instillation.
prophylaxis.target_population: Patients undergoing RNU for UTUC without a history of BC.
prophylaxis.duration: A single dose 2–10 days after surgery.

prophylaxis.recommendation: Before antegrade or retrograde upper urinary tract instillation, obtain a nephro-ureterogram to exclude ureteric obstruction or leakage, check that infection is absent and maintain a low-pressure system to avoid pyelovenous influx.
prophylaxis.target_population: Patients undergoing upper urinary tract instillation after kidney-sparing management.

infection_management.prevention: Before upper urinary tract instillation, check that infection is absent.

conditions.name: upper urinary tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC)
conditions.description: Urothelial carcinoma arising in the pyelocaliceal cavities or ureter. Histological grade often guides clinical decisions because biopsy samples may not reliably distinguish non-invasive papillary lesions, carcinoma in situ and invasive carcinoma. Pure non-urothelial histology is uncommon, while histological subtypes occur in approximately 25% of UTUCs.
conditions.epidemiology: UTUC accounts for 5–10% of urothelial carcinomas, with an estimated annual incidence in Western countries of almost two cases per 100,000 inhabitants. Incidence peaks at 70–90 years, and the disease is twice as common in men. Approximately two-thirds of patients present with muscle-invasive disease, although population-based studies suggest that muscle-invasive UTUC has represented approximately half of incident cases in recent years; approximately 9% present with metastasis. Pyelocaliceal tumours occur approximately twice as often as ureteral tumours. Multifocal tumours occur in approximately 10–20% of cases, concomitant upper-tract carcinoma in situ in 11% to 36%, and concurrent bladder cancer in 17%. After treatment, bladder recurrence occurs in 29% of patients, compared with contralateral upper-tract recurrence in 2–5%. Tobacco exposure increases relative risk by 2.5 to 7.0 fold; aristolochic acid exposure is another established risk factor. An association with alcohol was reported in a case-control study of 1,569 cases and 506,797 controls: ever-drinkers had higher risk than never-drinkers (OR: 1.23; 95% CI: 1.08–1.40, p = 0.001), with a reported risk threshold of > 15 g of alcohol/day.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Detection may be incidental. Most patients in an international registry presented with symptoms, principally visible haematuria; flank pain caused by obstruction from a clot or tumour tissue occurs in 20–32% of cases. Anorexia, weight loss, malaise, fatigue, fever, night sweats or cough should prompt assessment for metastases. Symptoms at diagnosis are associated with poorer prognosis.

subtypes.name: Low-risk UTUC
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Requires unifocal disease, tumour size < 2 cm, negative high-grade cytology, low-grade URS biopsy and no invasive appearance on CT; all listed factors must be present.

subtypes.name: High-risk UTUC
subtypes.distinguishing_features: High-grade cytology, high-grade URS biopsy, local invasion on CT or a histological subtype each constitute a strong high-risk criterion. Multifocal disease, tumour size ≥ 2 cm and hydronephrosis are weaker criteria and, in a low-grade tumour, are not strong predictors of invasion when considered alone.

subtypes.name: Lynch-related UTUC
subtypes.distinguishing_features: UTUC associated with Lynch syndrome and a pathogenic germline mismatch-repair gene mutation.

subtypes.name: upper tract CIS
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Flat carcinoma in situ of the upper urinary tract; its lack of a mass effect or urothelial thickening can make it invisible on CT.

subtypes.name: metastatic UTUC
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Disease with regional nodal involvement or distant metastases, for which the guideline describes separate management pathways.

subtypes.name: squamous subtype
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Urothelial carcinoma with divergent squamous differentiation, present in approximately 15% of cases.

subtypes.name: sarcomatoid
subtypes.distinguishing_features: A rare histological subtype associated with locally advanced disease and poorer outcomes.

subtypes.name: micropapillary
subtypes.distinguishing_features: A histological subtype associated with locally advanced disease and poorer outcomes.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Diagnose and stage UTUC, assess local invasion and examine regional lymph nodes.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: In the diagnostic and staging evaluation.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A meta-analysis of 13 studies involving 1,233 patients reported pooled sensitivity of 92% (CI: 0.85–0.96) and specificity of 95% (CI: 0.88–0.98). Enlarged lymph nodes strongly predict metastases. Flat epithelial lesions without a mass effect or urothelial thickening are generally not visible.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess for thoracic metastatic disease.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During staging and the specified follow-up of high-risk disease.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Provide upper-tract imaging when CT urography cannot be performed.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Usually when radiation or iodinated contrast is contraindicated.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Sensitivity after contrast administration is 75% for tumours < 2 cm; CT urography is more sensitive and specific for diagnosis and staging.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess nodal or distant metastases.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: May be used when iodinated contrast cannot be given because of renal impairment or allergy.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A retrospective multicentre study of 117 surgically treated patients reported sensitivity of 82% and specificity of 84% for nodal metastases. Suspicious nodes were associated with worse recurrence-free survival; further validation and comparison with MR and CT are needed.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Exclude a concurrent bladder tumour.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: As part of the UTUC diagnostic evaluation.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Help detect high-grade disease.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During diagnostic evaluation and, where specified, surveillance.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Abnormal cytology can suggest high-grade UTUC if cystoscopy is normal and bladder or prostatic-urethral CIS is absent. It is less sensitive for UTUC than selectively collected upper-tract cytology.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess the affected upper tract, particularly for high-grade tumours and CIS.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When upper-tract sampling is undertaken, including during URS.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Selective cytology has high sensitivity in high-grade disease, including CIS.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Obtain cytological material from the renal cavities and ureteral lumen.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Preferably before contrast administration for retrograde ureteropyelography.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: One study detected up to 91% of cancers; contrast can impair cytological specimens.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Provide an additional means of detecting UTUC.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: As a diagnostic option.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Visualise suspicious lesions, confirm diagnosis, map tumour presence, appearance, multifocality and size, and establish biopsy grade.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When imaging and voided cytology do not adequately establish the diagnosis or risk category, or before considering kidney-sparing management.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Biopsy establishes grade in more than 90% of cases, but can undergrade disease relative to nephroureterectomy specimens, and biopsy-based stage assessment can be inaccurate. URS with biopsy significantly increased subsequent intravesical recurrence in a systematic review of 16 studies, without an observed effect on overall survival or non-urothelial recurrence.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Detect molecular abnormalities characteristic of UTUC.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: As a possible ancillary urinary test.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Reported sensitivity for characteristic molecular abnormalities is approximately 72–84%. A systematic review reported sensitivity of 35-86% and specificity of 80-100%; the review concluded that available cytology and FISH performance was suboptimal for ruling out UTUC.

diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Assessed in a prospective study of 79 patients immediately before URS; not established as a routine test in the guideline.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The study reported sensitivity of 100% and specificity of 4%.

diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Further prospective comparative validation is needed.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: In a prospective study of 79 patients, sensitivity was 64% and specificity was 79%.

Mutations are depleted in low-grade tumours, whereas high-grade tumours often have alterations in TP53 signalling.

staging.additional_rules: Regional nodes comprise hilar and retroperitoneal nodes and, for mid- and distal-ureteral tumours, pelvic nodes. Laterality does not change the N classification.

risk_groups.criteria: All of the following: unifocal disease, tumour size < 2 cm, negative high-grade cytology, low-grade URS biopsy and no invasive appearance on CT.
risk_groups.expected_outcome: Identifies patients more likely to be suitable for kidney-sparing treatment.

risk_groups.criteria: Any strong criterion—high-grade cytology, high-grade URS biopsy, local invasion on CT or a histological subtype—supports high-risk classification. Multifocal disease, tumour size ≥ 2 cm and hydronephrosis are weak criteria that should be considered alongside other factors.
risk_groups.expected_outcome: Identifies patients at greater risk of progression to > pT2 or non-organ-confined disease.

prognostic_tools.interpretation: Multifocality, size or hydronephrosis alone is insufficient to determine risk, particularly with low-grade disease. Their value as individual surrogates of high-risk progression has a low level of evidence.

prognostic_tools.name: American Society of Anesthesiologists [ASA]
prognostic_tools.interpretation: A higher score is associated with worse cancer-specific survival after RNU; the guideline does not provide scoring thresholds.

prognostic_tools.name: Charlson Comorbidity Index
prognostic_tools.interpretation: Higher comorbidity indices are associated with poorer survival across disease stages; the guideline does not provide scoring thresholds.

prognostic_tools.name: modified Glasgow score
prognostic_tools.interpretation: Mentioned among blood-based measures associated with locally advanced disease and cancer-specific mortality; no components or cut-offs are specified.

prognostic_tools.name: De Ritis ratio
prognostic_tools.interpretation: A high ratio has been associated with locally advanced disease and cancer-specific mortality; no cut-off is specified.

follow_up.schedule: Follow-up is determined by risk category and prior treatment; schedules are specified in the corresponding low-risk and high-risk entries.
follow_up.survivorship_notes: Surveillance aims to address rehabilitation needs and detect new or recurrent urothelial tumours and regional or distant metastases. The evidence underlying follow-up recommendations is limited by substantial heterogeneity. Bladder recurrence is not classified as distant recurrence.

conditions.name: Low-risk UTUC
conditions.description: Localised UTUC meeting all the guideline's low-risk features. This category identifies patients for whom kidney-sparing management is the preferred primary approach.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess tumour extent and confirm the absence of an invasive appearance.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During initial risk stratification and scheduled follow-up.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: An invasive appearance is incompatible with the listed low-risk criteria.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess for high-grade disease.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During initial risk stratification.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Cytology must be negative for high-grade disease to meet the low-risk criteria.

diagnostic_workup.test: URS with biopsy and tumour mapping
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Determine grade, focality and size before considering kidney-sparing management.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When necessary for diagnosis or risk stratification.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Low-grade biopsy is a required low-risk feature. Diagnostic biopsy can undergrade disease.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify residual tumour or a change in stage or grade after kidney-sparing treatment.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Early after endoscopic kidney-sparing management.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The follow-up schedule described for low-risk disease applies where the early assessment or segmental-resection specimen does not reveal upstaging or upgrading.

pathology_markers.clinical_significance: A required feature of the low-risk category.

staging.additional_rules: The clinical low-risk category requires no invasive appearance on CT; it is not itself a TNM stage.

prognostic_tools.name: Risk stratification of non-metastatic UTUC according to the risk of progression to a> pT2 /nonorgan-confined disease

risk_groups.criteria: Every listed component must be present.

prognostic_tools.interpretation: Multifocality, hydronephrosis or tumour size alone does not establish high-risk disease when other findings indicate a low-grade tumour.

follow_up.schedule: After RNU, perform cystoscopy at three months; if negative, repeat 9 months later and then yearly for 5 years. After kidney-sparing management, perform cystoscopy and CT urography at 3 and 6 months and then yearly for 5 years. An early second-look ureteroscopy is described after 6-8 weeks; perform URS at 3 months if no second-look examination was performed.
follow_up.survivorship_notes: Metastasis screening after RNU is not mandatory, and routine contralateral upper-tract imaging should be decided individually because recurrence risk there is low. After kidney-sparing management, the reported risk of bladder recurrence beyond 5 years is 6%.

conditions.name: High-risk UTUC
conditions.description: UTUC with a strong high-risk feature or a combination of concerning findings. The guideline identifies radical nephroureterectomy as standard treatment for non-metastatic high-risk disease.

subtypes.name: histological subtype
subtypes.distinguishing_features: A strong high-risk criterion; subtypes are associated with poorer survival than pure urothelial carcinoma.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess invasion, tumour extent and regional nodes.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: For diagnosis, staging and follow-up.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Local invasion is a strong high-risk criterion; hydronephrosis is a weaker criterion.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Monitor for thoracic metastatic disease.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: At the specified post-RNU surveillance intervals.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Detect high-grade disease and support surveillance.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: At diagnosis and during follow-up.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: High-grade cytology is a strong high-risk criterion.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Determine tumour grade and map lesions when needed for risk stratification.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When imaging and voided cytology are insufficient.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A high-grade biopsy is a strong high-risk criterion, although biopsy may undergrade tumour.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess TNM stage, subtype, lymphovascular invasion, nodal involvement and margins.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: After resection.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: These findings inform prognosis and consideration of subsequent treatment.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify residual tumour after kidney-sparing treatment.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: In 6 weeks after kidney-sparing management of high-risk disease.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: If no residual tumour is found, subsequent surveillance follows principles similar to those after RNU for high-risk disease.

pathology_markers.expected_result: High-grade cytology or high-grade URS biopsy can establish a strong high-risk criterion.
pathology_markers.clinical_significance: One of the main prognostic factors.
A strong high-risk criterion associated with worse cancer-specific and overall survival.
An independent survival predictor that should be documented.

staging.additional_rules: High-risk status is a clinical progression-risk category rather than a separate TNM stage.

prognostic_tools.name: Risk stratification of non-metastatic UTUC according to the risk of progression to a> pT2 /nonorgan-confined disease

risk_groups.criteria: Any strong criterion—high-grade cytology, high-grade URS biopsy, local invasion on CT or histological subtype—supports this category. Multifocal disease, tumour size ≥ 2 cm and hydronephrosis are weak criteria requiring interpretation with other findings.
risk_groups.expected_outcome: Higher risk of progression to > pT2 or non-organ-confined disease.

prognostic_tools.interpretation: A weak criterion alone is insufficient for risk classification, particularly with low-grade disease; the guideline calls for shared decision-making in this situation.

follow_up.schedule: After RNU, perform cystoscopy and urinary cytology at 3 months. If negative, repeat both every 3 months for 2 years, every 6 months thereafter until 5 years, and then yearly. Perform CT urography and chest CT every 6 months for 2 years and then yearly. After kidney-sparing management, perform second-look URS and cytology in 6 weeks; if no residual tumour is found, use follow-up principles similar to those after RNU for high-risk disease.
follow_up.survivorship_notes: Careful, long-term surveillance of the ipsilateral upper tract is needed after kidney-sparing treatment because recurrence risk is high, and progression can occur even beyond 5 years. After RNU, bladder and other-site recurrence risks decrease 4 years after surgery. The reason for kidney-sparing treatment, including whether it was imperative, affects the consequences of recurrence.

conditions.name: Lynch-related UTUC
conditions.description: UTUC occurring in association with Lynch syndrome, a hereditary predisposition linked to pathogenic germline mismatch-repair gene mutations. Identification has implications for the patient's risk of additional malignancies and for relatives.
conditions.epidemiology: UTUC is the 3rd most common malignancy in the Lynch syndrome spectrum after colorectal and endometrial cancer. Germline MMR mutations were reported in 9% of patients with UTUC, compared with 1% of patients with bladder cancer. Most associated tumours arise in carriers of MSH2 or MSH6 mutations. In a study of 115 consecutive patients with UTUC, 13.9% screened positive for possible Lynch syndrome by Amsterdam II criteria and 5.2% had confirmed Lynch syndrome.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Patients testing positive for Lynch syndrome are significantly younger and more often have ureteral UTUC. An initial UTUC diagnosis at age <60, a personal history of a Lynch-related malignancy or specified affected first-degree relatives can raise suspicion. No effect of Lynch syndrome on UTUC prognosis has been demonstrated to date.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify clinical suspicion of hereditary UTUC during the first medical interview.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Through systematic assessment of personal and family history in patients with UTUC.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The simplified UTUC screening features shown are age < 60 yr, a personal history of Lynch-spectrum cancer, one first-degree relative < 50 yr with Lynch-spectrum cancer, or two first-degree relatives with Lynch-spectrum cancer.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify families at increased risk of Lynch syndrome.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When assessing personal and family history.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Criteria include at least three relatives with an associated cancer, one being a first-degree relative of the other two; at least two successive affected generations; at least one diagnosis before age 50; exclusion of familial adenomatous polyposis in colorectal cancer cases; and pathological confirmation.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Estimate an individual's cumulative probability of carrying a germline mutation associated with Lynch syndrome.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The model is described, although Amsterdam II criteria remain the predominantly used approach for identifying higher-risk families.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify loss of mismatch-repair protein expression indicative of dMMR.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Testing can be offered even without clinical suspicion of hereditary UTUC.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Loss of expression of the corresponding MLH1, MSH2, MSH6 or PMS2 protein can indicate dMMR. A positive test should prompt germline sequencing and family counselling.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Detect microsatellite instability associated with deficient mismatch repair.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Testing can be offered even without clinical suspicion of hereditary UTUC.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A positive result should prompt germline sequencing and family counselling.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess for an inherited mutation associated with hereditary UTUC.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When hereditary UTUC is clinically suspected or tumour MMR/MSI screening is positive.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The screening flowchart reports a mutation in 5–9%.

A first-degree relationship between one affected relative and the other two

prognostic_tools.interpretation: Predominantly used to identify families at increased risk, although clinical criteria have limited diagnostic performance.

components: One first-degree relative < 50 yr with Lynch-spectrum cancer

risk_groups.criteria: Presence of a listed personal or family-history screening feature.
risk_groups.expected_outcome: The proposed simplified screening tool could identify more than 20% of patients with UTUC as having suspected Lynch-related disease.

prognostic_tools.interpretation: High clinical suspicion prompts germline sequencing and family counselling. Patients without clinical suspicion may nevertheless benefit from tumour MMR or MSI screening.

follow_up.survivorship_notes: The guideline states that an optimal long-term screening and follow-up strategy for people with Lynch syndrome, with or without UTUC, is unknown. Urinalysis for non-visible haematuria and urine cytology are inadequate surveillance approaches, particularly for MSH2 mutation carriers and people who have already developed UTUC. Clinical evaluation for other Lynch-related cancers, close monitoring and familial genetic counselling are shown in its screening pathway.

conditions.name: upper tract CIS
synonyms: carcinoma in situ of the upper tract
conditions.description: A flat carcinoma in situ lesion in the upper urinary tract. The guideline discusses its assessment and upper-tract instillation after kidney-sparing tumour eradication.
conditions.epidemiology: Concomitant carcinoma in situ of the upper tract is reported in 11% to 36% of UTUC cases.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess the upper tract and other disease features.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During UTUC evaluation.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A flat epithelial lesion without mass effect or urothelial thickening generally cannot be seen on CT.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Detect high-grade disease, including CIS.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During diagnostic assessment.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The guideline describes high sensitivity for high-grade tumours, including CIS.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Visualise and sample suspicious upper-tract lesions.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When needed to establish diagnosis or risk.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Biopsy sampling can make flat lesions difficult to distinguish reliably from other tumour categories.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Exclude obstruction or leakage before an upper-tract instillation.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Before antegrade or retrograde upper-tract instillation.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The assessment should also establish that infection is absent and the system has low pressure.

follow_up.survivorship_notes: Concomitant CIS in organ-confined UTUC is associated with increased recurrence and cancer-specific mortality. The guideline does not specify a separate CIS-only follow-up calendar.

conditions.name: clinically N+ UTUC
conditions.description: UTUC with clinically identified loco-regional lymph-node metastases. The guideline notes that evidence is lacking on its optimal management.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess regional nodal enlargement and disease extent.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During staging.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Enlarged lymph nodes on CT strongly predict metastases.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Evaluate suspected nodal metastases.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: May be used when iodinated contrast cannot be administered.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: A retrospective multicentre study reported sensitivity of 82% and specificity of 84% for nodal metastases; suspicious nodes were associated with worse recurrence-free survival.

pathology_markers.clinical_significance: A cut-off of 30% is reported as a predictor of survival in N+ UTUC.
Predicts survival outcomes in N+ UTUC.

definitions.description: Metastasis in one lymph node measuring 2 cm or less in its greatest dimension.
Metastasis in one lymph node measuring more than 2 cm, or in multiple lymph nodes.

staging.additional_rules: Hilar and retroperitoneal lymph nodes are regional; pelvic nodes are also regional for mid- and distal-ureteral tumours. Laterality does not affect N classification.

follow_up.survivorship_notes: The guideline does not provide a separate surveillance calendar for clinically node-positive disease.

conditions.name: metastatic UTUC
conditions.description: UTUC with distant metastatic disease. The guideline separates initial and subsequent systemic-treatment decisions according to fitness for combination therapy, prior treatments and, for certain later treatments, tumour biomarkers.
conditions.epidemiology: Approximately 9% of patients with UTUC present with metastasis.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Systemic features that warrant assessment for metastases include anorexia, weight loss, malaise, fatigue, fever, night sweats and cough.
