therapies_index.name: kidney-sparing surgery
approved_indications: Preferred primary approach for low-risk UTUC.
May be considered individually for high-risk UTUC when an imperative indication makes radical nephroureterectomy unsuitable.
key_toxicities: For high-risk UTUC, disease progression is more likely than after kidney-sparing surgery for low-risk UTUC.
monitoring: Early second-look ureteroscopy and stringent surveillance are required after endoscopic treatment.
The ipsilateral upper urinary tract requires careful, long-term follow-up after kidney-sparing treatment of high-risk UTUC.

therapies_index.name: endoscopic ablation
approved_indications: Consider for clinically low-risk UTUC.
therapies_index.administration: The tumour must be completely resected or destroyed.
key_toxicities: Local recurrence and repeated interventions are more frequent than after radical nephroureterectomy.
monitoring: Early second-look URS and stringent surveillance.

therapies_index.name: ureteroscopy
approved_indications: Endoscopic kidney-sparing treatment of suitable low-risk UTUC.
May be considered for high-risk UTUC with an imperative indication for kidney preservation.
therapies_index.administration: A flexible ureteroscope can be used to manage pelvicalyceal tumours.
monitoring: Early second-look URS and stringent surveillance after endoscopic management.

therapies_index.name: percutaneous management
approved_indications: May be considered for low-risk UTUC of the renal pelvis, including lower caliceal tumours that are inaccessible or difficult to treat with flexible URS.
therapies_index.administration: Percutaneous access to the upper urinary tract.

therapies_index.name: segmental ureteral resection
approved_indications: Kidney-preserving resection of suitable ureteral tumours.
May be considered individually for high-risk UTUC with an imperative indication for kidney preservation.
therapies_index.administration: Resect the affected ureteral segment with adequate margins while preserving the ipsilateral kidney.
key_toxicities: Resection in the proximal two-thirds of the ureter has higher failure rates than distal ureteral resection.

therapies_index.name: distal ureterectomy
approved_indications: Low-risk distal ureteral tumours that cannot be removed completely by endoscopy.
Selected high-risk tumours confined to the distal ureter.
therapies_index.administration: For low-risk tumours, distal ureterectomy is performed with ureteroneocystostomy. Concomitant LN dissection is possible for selected high-risk tumours.

therapies_index.name: ureteroneocystostomy
approved_indications: Reconstruction accompanying distal ureterectomy for a low-risk distal ureteral tumour that cannot be completely removed endoscopically.

therapies_index.name: total ureterectomy
approved_indications: Selected low-risk cases in which a kidney-preserving procedure is mandatory.
therapies_index.administration: May be combined with ileal-ureteral substitution or renal autotransplantation with pyelocystostomy.

therapies_index.name: ileal-ureteral substitution
approved_indications: Selected low-risk cases requiring kidney preservation after total ureterectomy.

therapies_index.name: renal autotransplantation with pyelocystostomy
approved_indications: Selected low-risk cases requiring kidney preservation after total ureterectomy.

therapies_index.name: radical nephroureterectomy
approved_indications: Standard treatment for high-risk non-metastatic UTUC regardless of tumour location.
May be offered as palliation for symptomatic, resectable locally-advanced tumours.
therapies_index.administration: Remove the kidney and ureter en bloc with the bladder cuff, following oncological precautions against tumour seeding.
key_toxicities: Loss of kidney function may prevent subsequent cisplatin treatment.
Bladder recurrence after RNU occurs in 22–47% of patients with UTUC.
monitoring: Follow-up depends on tumour risk and includes cystoscopy, with additional urinary cytology and imaging for high-risk disease.

therapies_index.name: open RNU
approved_indications: Preferred approach for non-organ-confined UTUC and favoured for invasive or large (T3/T4 and/or N+/M+) tumours.
therapies_index.administration: Open radical nephroureterectomy with bladder cuff excision.

therapies_index.name: laparoscopic RNU
approved_indications: A surgical approach for UTUC when strict oncological principles can be followed by an experienced team.
therapies_index.administration: Avoid tumour contact and spillage, use a closed system and an endobag, avoid morcellation, and remove the kidney, ureter and bladder cuff en bloc.
key_toxicities: Retroperitoneal dissemination and trocar-pathway metastasis may occur after manipulation of large tumours.
Intravesical recurrence may be more frequent than after open RNU.

therapies_index.name: robot-assisted laparoscopic approach
approved_indications: May be considered as an approach to RNU.
key_toxicities: Intravesical recurrence may be more frequent than after open RNU.

therapies_index.name: bladder cuff excision
approved_indications: Removal of the distal ureter and its orifice as part of RNU.
therapies_index.administration: Complete excision of the bladder cuff.
key_toxicities: Incomplete removal increases the risk of bladder cancer recurrence.

therapies_index.name: lymph node dissection
approved_indications: Offer template-based dissection to patients undergoing RNU for high-risk non-metastatic UTUC.
May accompany selected distal ureterectomies or resection of responsive clinical nodal disease.
therapies_index.administration: A template-based, complete dissection is described for RNU.

therapies_index.name: metastasectomy
approved_indications: May be considered individually for selected patients with advanced disease after shared decision-making; UTUC-specific supporting studies are absent.
therapies_index.administration: Surgical resection of metastatic lesions.

therapies_index.name: mitomycin-containing reverse thermal gel (UGN-101)
approved_indications: Investigated for chemo-ablation of biopsy-proven low-grade UTUC less than 15 mm.
therapies_index.administration: In the cited trial, instillation into the renal pelvis and calyces through a retrograde catheter comprised 6 weekly induction treatments.
key_toxicities: In the cited trial, all-cause adverse events included ureteric stenosis in 31 (44%), urinary tract infection in 23 (32%), haematuria in 22 (31%), flank pain in 21 (30%) and nausea in 17 (24%). Of patients with ureteric stenosis, 19/31 (61%) required treatment.

therapies_index.name: mitomycin C
approved_indications: Studied as an upper-tract adjuvant instillation after complete tumour eradication in kidney-sparing management of CIS.
Studied as an early, single upper-tract instillation after treatment of low-grade UTUC; a possible reduction in local recurrence requires further randomised evaluation.
Studied as a single postoperative intravesical chemotherapy instillation after RNU in patients without a history of BC.
therapies_index.administration: Upper-tract instillation has been given antegrade through a percutaneous nephrostomy or retrograde through a single-J open-ended ureteric stent. A single postoperative intravesical dose has been given 2–10 days after RNU.
monitoring: Before upper-tract instillation, exclude ureteric obstruction or leakage and infection, and ensure a low-pressure system.

therapies_index.name: BCG
approved_indications: Studied as an upper-tract instillation for CIS after complete tumour eradication with kidney-sparing management.
therapies_index.administration: Upper-tract instillation has been given antegrade through a percutaneous nephrostomy or retrograde through a single-J open-ended ureteric stent.
monitoring: Before instillation, exclude ureteric obstruction or leakage and infection, and ensure a low-pressure system.

therapies_index.name: pirarubicin
approved_indications: Studied as a single postoperative intravesical chemotherapy dose after RNU in patients without a history of BC.
therapies_index.administration: A single intravesical dose 2–10 days after surgery was evaluated.

therapies_index.name: intravesical chemotherapy
approved_indications: A single postoperative instillation is recommended after RNU to reduce bladder recurrence in patients without a history of BC.
Evidence does not currently support bladder instillation after kidney-sparing surgery.
therapies_index.administration: A single dose may be given 2–10 days after RNU. Administration during RNU before opening the bladder cuff has also been reported, but efficacy data for that timing are limited.
key_toxicities: The studies of a single postoperative instillation reported a very low risk of adverse events.
monitoring: Consider a cystogram before postoperative instillation if drug extravasation is a concern.

therapies_index.name: bladder irrigation
approved_indications: A study with low-level evidence suggested that irrigation might lower bladder recurrence after RNU.

therapies_index.name: cisplatin
approved_indications: A component of combination chemotherapy before or after RNU and for eligible patients with advanced or metastatic UTUC.
therapies_index.administration: Split dosing with hydration may be considered at a GFR down to 45 mL/min.
monitoring: Assess renal function when determining eligibility, particularly after RNU.

therapies_index.name: carboplatin
approved_indications: A component of combination chemotherapy for patients unsuitable for cisplatin.
The guide states that carboplatin is not indicated for neoadjuvant treatment.
monitoring: Assess platinum eligibility, including GFR and ECOG PS.

therapies_index.name: gemcitabine
approved_indications: A component of the platinum-based combination regimens described for adjuvant and advanced or metastatic treatment.

therapies_index.name: gemcitabine/cisplatin
approved_indications: Recommended first-line chemotherapy for cisplatin-eligible patients with advanced or metastatic disease who are unsuitable for Enfortumab + Pembrolizumab.
Used as adjuvant platinum-based chemotherapy after RNU in eligible patients.
therapies_index.administration: The cited adjuvant trial evaluated four cycles initiated within 90 days after RNU.
monitoring: Assess cisplatin eligibility and renal function.

therapies_index.name: gemcitabine/carboplatin
approved_indications: Recommended chemotherapy for cisplatin-ineligible patients with advanced or metastatic disease who are unsuitable for Enfortumab + Pembrolizumab.
Used as adjuvant platinum-based chemotherapy after RNU in eligible patients.
therapies_index.administration: The cited adjuvant trial evaluated four cycles initiated within 90 days after RNU.
monitoring: Assess platinum eligibility and renal function.

therapies_index.name: HD-MVAC
approved_indications: Recommended as a cisplatin-based chemotherapy option for cisplatin-eligible patients with advanced or metastatic disease who are unsuitable for Enfortumab + Pembrolizumab.

therapies_index.name: methotrexate
approved_indications: Named as a component of HD-MVAC and of a chemotherapy regimen cited in the references.

therapies_index.name: vinblastine
approved_indications: Named as a component of HD-MVAC and of a chemotherapy regimen cited in the references.

therapies_index.name: adriamycin
approved_indications: Named as a component of HD-MVAC.

therapies_index.name: neoadjuvant chemotherapy
approved_indications: Cisplatin-based combination treatment before RNU has been studied for high-grade and/or cT2-T4N0M0 UTUC.
therapies_index.administration: Given before RNU while renal function may still permit cisplatin use.

therapies_index.name: pembrolizumab
approved_indications: In combination with enfortumab vedotin, recommended as first-line treatment for advanced or metastatic disease.
An option for PD-L1-positive patients ineligible for any combination therapy.
Recommended after progression during or after platinum-based combination chemotherapy for metastatic disease in patients who did not receive maintenance avelumab.
A small neoadjuvant study in high-risk UTUC found no pathological response; the guide states that evidence does not currently support neoadjuvant immunotherapy in this setting.
key_toxicities: The cited neoadjuvant study reported one treatment-related death; no pathological response was observed.

therapies_index.name: enfortumab vedotin
therapies_index.mechanism: Described as a nectin 4-directed antibody–drug conjugate.
approved_indications: In combination with pembrolizumab, recommended as first-line treatment for advanced or metastatic disease.
Recommended after platinum-containing chemotherapy when disease progresses during or after treatment with a PD-1 or PD-L1 inhibitor.

therapies_index.name: Enfortumab vedotin in combination with pembrolizumab
therapies_index.mechanism: Combines a nectin 4-directed antibody–drug conjugate with a checkpoint inhibitor.
approved_indications: Recommended first-line treatment for advanced or metastatic disease.
key_toxicities: In the cited EV302 study, grade 3 or above treatment-related adverse events of special interest included skin reactions (15.5%), peripheral neuropathy (6.8%) and hyperglycaemia (6.1%).

therapies_index.name: nivolumab
approved_indications: EMA-approved as adjuvant monotherapy for high-risk muscle-invasive UC after radical surgery when tumour-cell PD-L1 expression is > 1% and the patient declines or is unfit for adjuvant chemotherapy.

The guide recommends discussing adjuvant treatment after RNU for specified high-risk patients who decline or are unfit for platinum-based adjuvant chemotherapy; the UTUC subgroup in the cited trial did not appear to benefit and needs further analysis.
Recommended with gemcitabine-cisplatin as a first-line option for cisplatin-eligible patients unsuitable for Enfortumab + Pembrolizumab.
key_toxicities: In the cited adjuvant trial, treatment-related adverse events > grade 3 occurred in 17.9% of the nivolumab group.

therapies_index.name: gemcitabine-cisplatin + nivolumab
approved_indications: Recommended as a first-line option for cisplatin-eligible patients with advanced or metastatic disease who are unsuitable for Enfortumab + Pembrolizumab.

therapies_index.name: avelumab
approved_indications: Recommended as first-line maintenance for patients without progression after 4 to 6 cycles of platinum-based combination chemotherapy.
May be offered as maintenance after response or stable disease following first-line platinum-based chemotherapy for clinically node-positive UTUC.
therapies_index.administration: In the cited maintenance trial, treatment began within 10 weeks of completing first-line platinum-based chemotherapy. The guide states that data do not support maintenance avelumab outside the first-line setting.
monitoring: Confirm that disease has not progressed after first-line platinum-based chemotherapy.

therapies_index.name: atezolizumab
approved_indications: An option for PD-L1-positive patients with advanced or metastatic disease who are ineligible for any combination therapy.
monitoring: Confirm PD-L1-positive tumour status for the first-line use described.

therapies_index.name: erdafitinib
therapies_index.mechanism: Described as a pan-FGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor of FGFR1–4.
approved_indications: Recommended as an alternative subsequent-line therapy after platinum-containing chemotherapy and progression during or after a PD-1 or PD-L1 inhibitor, when FGFR DNA genomic alterations (FGFR2/3 mutations or FGFR3 fusions) are present.
monitoring: Test for FGFR alterations (FGFR2/3 mutations or FGFR3 fusions) before treatment.

therapies_index.name: sacituzumab govitecan
therapies_index.mechanism: Described as an antibody–drug conjugate; its target is not specified.
approved_indications: Listed among possible later-line treatments in the metastatic-disease flowchart after prior systemic therapy.

therapies_index.name: paclitaxel
approved_indications: Listed as a possible later-line single-agent chemotherapy option in the metastatic-disease flowchart.

therapies_index.name: docetaxel
approved_indications: Listed as a possible later-line single-agent chemotherapy option in the metastatic-disease flowchart.

therapies_index.name: vinflunine
approved_indications: Recommended as second-line treatment for metastatic disease only when immunotherapy or combination chemotherapy is not feasible.
Alternatively recommended in the third or a subsequent line.

therapies_index.name: ipilimumab
approved_indications: Studied with nivolumab after progression on platinum-based chemotherapy; the guide notes that data on later-line immunotherapy combinations remain limited.

therapies_index.name: nivolumab plus ipilimumab
approved_indications: Investigated in metastatic UC progressing after platinum-based chemotherapy; the cited trial did not provide a UTUC subgroup analysis.

therapies_index.name: durvalumab
approved_indications: Investigated for platinum-resistant metastatic UC in a single-arm early-phase trial; no UTUC-specific subgroup analysis is reported.

therapies_index.name: ramucirumab
approved_indications: Studied with docetaxel after progression on platinum-based chemotherapy and immune checkpoint inhibitors; the guide says the subgroup findings require confirmation.

therapies_index.name: ramucirumab/docetaxel
approved_indications: Investigated after progression on platinum-based chemotherapy and immune checkpoint inhibitors; the guide states that the subgroup findings need confirmation.

therapies_index.name: adjuvant radiation therapy
approved_indications: Suggested for locoregional control after surgery, but the guide considers the evidence controversial and insufficient for conclusions.
therapies_index.administration: After surgical removal of the tumour.

therapies_index.name: best supportive care
approved_indications: Shown as an option in the metastatic-disease flowchart.

special_populations.population: Patients with Lynch syndrome or suspected hereditary UTUC
special_populations.considerations: Lynch syndrome predisposes carriers to UTUC and other malignancies, with implications for relatives. Patients meeting clinical criteria for hereditary UTUC should undergo germline DNA sequencing and family counselling. Patients without clinical suspicion may be tested for MSI or dMMR; a positive result should also prompt germline sequencing and family counselling. The optimal long-term screening and follow-up strategy remains unknown.

special_populations.population: Patients with high-risk UTUC and imperative indications for kidney preservation
special_populations.considerations: A solitary kidney, bilateral UTUC, severe chronic kidney disease or another comorbidity that compromises RNU may make kidney preservation necessary. Kidney-sparing treatment carries a greater risk of progression in high-risk than in low-risk UTUC, with an effect on survival.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Discuss kidney-sparing management, including ureteroscopy or segmental ureterectomy, individually through shared decision-making despite the greater progression risk.

special_populations.population: Patients unable to undergo CT urography
special_populations.considerations: Radiation or iodinated contrast media may contraindicate CT urography. Renal impairment or allergy may prevent the use of iodinated contrast media.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Magnetic resonance urography or 18F-Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/CT may be used when CT is contraindicated. FDG-PET can also assess nodal and distant metastases when iodinated contrast media cannot be used.

special_populations.population: Patients with a history of BC
special_populations.considerations: Previous BC is associated with a higher risk of UTUC, and a history of BC is a predictor of bladder recurrence after RNU. The trials supporting a single post-operative intravesical chemotherapy instillation after RNU enrolled patients without a history of BC.

special_populations.population: Patients with metastatic disease who are ineligible for EV+Pembro and unfit for cisplatin-based combination chemotherapy
special_populations.considerations: Eligibility for platinum-based treatment depends on performance status, renal function and other criteria specified in the guideline.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Carboplatin-based chemotherapy is recommended for patients unfit for cisplatin; carboplatin with gemcitabine is the preferred regimen irrespective of PDL-1 status.

special_populations.population: Patients with metastatic disease who are ineligible for any combination therapy
special_populations.considerations: For patients in this group with PD-L1-positive tumours, the guideline identifies single-agent checkpoint inhibitors as treatment options.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Offer pembrolizumab or atezolizumab to patients with PD-L1-positive tumours.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients meeting all low-risk criteria: unifocal disease, tumour size < 2 cm, negative high-grade cytology, low-grade URS biopsy and no invasive appearance on CT.
decision_rules: Offer kidney-sparing management as the primary treatment and discuss it with every patient with low-risk disease, regardless of contralateral kidney status.

Multifocality, hydroureteronephrosis or tumour size alone does not establish high-risk disease when other high-risk factors are absent; use shared decision-making when low-grade disease has these features.
Select the kidney-sparing procedure according to tumour location and whether complete removal is feasible.

recommended_regimens.name: Kidney-sparing management
recommended_regimens.summary: Preferred initial approach for low-risk tumours; it preserves the kidney without compromising oncological outcomes relative to radical nephroureterectomy.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The guideline reports survival similar to that after RNU, while noting higher local recurrence and repeated interventions after endoscopic treatment in a systematic review.

response_assessment.method: Early second-look ureteroscopy after kidney-sparing treatment
response_assessment.interpretation: Check for residual disease or a higher stage or grade before following the low-risk surveillance schedule.

response_assessment.timepoint: 3 and 6 months, then yearly for 5 years
response_assessment.interpretation: The specified schedule applies if early assessment does not show upstaging or upgrading.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Patients considering endoscopic treatment must be willing and able to undergo an early second-look URS and close surveillance. Imaging and biopsy may inadequately characterise tumour risk, so progression remains possible.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with clinically low-risk tumours accessible to ureteroscopic treatment, including pelvicalyceal tumours.
decision_rules: Consider endoscopic ablation only if the tumour can be completely resected or destroyed.
Use flexible ureteroscopy for suitable pelvicalyceal lesions and arrange early second-look URS and stringent surveillance.

recommended_regimens.name: Endoscopic ablation
recommended_regimens.summary: A kidney-sparing option to consider for clinically low-risk disease when complete treatment and subsequent surveillance are feasible.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: A systematic review reported survival comparable to radical nephroureterectomy, but more local recurrences and repeat procedures; long-term preservation of renal function remained uncertain.

response_assessment.interpretation: Assess completeness of treatment and detect residual tumour or a higher stage or grade.

response_assessment.method: URS if second-look ureteroscopy was not performed

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Progression is possible because pretreatment imaging and biopsy do not perfectly establish stage or tumour biology.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with low-risk renal pelvis tumours, or low-risk lower caliceal tumours that are inaccessible or difficult to treat with flexible URS.
decision_rules: Consider percutaneous treatment for an appropriate renal pelvis lesion.
It may also be offered when a lower caliceal lesion is difficult to manage by flexible URS.

recommended_regimens.name: Percutaneous management
recommended_regimens.summary: A location-dependent kidney-sparing option for selected low-risk tumours.

response_assessment.method: Early second-look ureteroscopy after kidney-sparing treatment
response_assessment.interpretation: Evaluate for residual disease or a change in stage or grade.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Improved ureteroscopes have reduced use of percutaneous access; tumour seeding remains a potential risk.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with low-risk distal ureteral tumours that cannot be completely removed endoscopically.
decision_rules: Use distal ureterectomy with ureteroneocystostomy when complete endoscopic removal is not possible.
Segmental resection should obtain adequate margins while preserving the ipsilateral kidney.

recommended_regimens.name: Distal ureterectomy with ureteroneocystostomy
recommended_regimens.summary: Kidney-preserving resection indicated for an incompletely endoscopically removable low-risk distal ureteral tumour; the specimen also permits staging and grading.

alternative_regimens.name: Total ureterectomy with an ileal-ureteral substitution
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Only selected low-risk cases in which preservation of the kidney is mandatory.

alternative_regimens.name: Renal autotransplantation with pyelocystostomy
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Only selected low-risk cases in which preservation of the kidney is mandatory.

response_assessment.interpretation: Check for upstaging or upgrading before applying the low-risk follow-up schedule.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Segmental resection in the proximal two-thirds of the ureter has higher failure rates than distal ureteral resection.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with biopsy-confirmed low-grade UTUC less than 15 mm, as studied in a single-arm phase III trial.
decision_rules: Chemo-ablation with UGN-101 is a studied kidney-sparing option for this population; the described findings come from a single-arm trial.

alternative_regimens.name: UGN-101
alternative_regimens.summary: In a single-arm phase III trial of 71 patients, retrograde delivery of mitomycin-containing reverse thermal gel to the renal pelvis and calyces produced a complete response in 41 patients (58%). Among the 41 complete responders, 23/41 (56%) remained disease free at one year.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: The studied population had biopsy-confirmed low-grade UTUC less than 15 mm.

response_assessment.interpretation: The trial reported complete response in 41 patients (58%).
The trial reported that 23/41 (56%) remained disease free.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: In the trial, 29 complete responders received at least one maintenance instillation (median of 6). Reported all-cause adverse events included ureteric stenosis in 31 (44%), urinary tract infection in 23 (32%), haematuria in 22 (31%), flank pain in 21 (30%) and nausea in 17 (24%); 19/31 (61%) with ureteric stenosis required treatment.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with upper-tract CIS after complete tumour eradication and kidney-sparing management; evidence on adjuvant endocavitary treatment also includes papillary non-invasive (Ta–T1) UTUC.
decision_rules: Upper-tract BCG or mitomycin C instillation has been studied after kidney-sparing treatment, but the evidence does not establish its efficacy.
Before antegrade or retrograde instillation, use a nephro-ureterogram to exclude obstruction or leakage, establish that infection is absent and ensure a low-pressure system.

alternative_regimens.name: BCG
alternative_regimens.summary: Studied as upper-tract endocavitary treatment for CIS after kidney-sparing management, delivered antegradely through percutaneous nephrostomy or retrogradely through a single-J open-ended ureteric stent.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Consider only in the context of uncertain efficacy and the required pre-instillation checks.

alternative_regimens.name: mitomycin C
alternative_regimens.summary: Studied as an upper-tract adjuvant instillation after kidney-sparing management. Early single instillation in low-grade UTUC might reduce local recurrence, but this needs randomised evaluation.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Exclude leakage before instillation; evidence does not establish a routine adjuvant benefit.

not_recommended.name: Double-J stent reflux delivery
not_recommended.reason: This delivery approach is suboptimal because the instilled drug often fails to reach the renal pelvis.

supportive_care: Before upper-tract instillation, exclude ureteric obstruction, leakage and infection, and maintain a low-pressure system to avoid pyelovenous influx.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: A systematic review found no difference in recurrence, progression, CSS or OS by antegrade, retrograde or combined delivery, but its studies were small, underpowered and heterogeneous. Recurrence after adjuvant instillation was comparable to reports in untreated patients, calling efficacy into question. Data do not support bladder chemotherapy instillation after kidney-sparing surgery; the available RCTs enrolled patients who underwent RNU.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with high-risk non-metastatic UTUC, regardless of tumour location.
decision_rules: Offer RNU for high-risk non-metastatic disease, with complete removal of the distal ureter and bladder cuff.
Offer template-based lymphadenectomy when RNU is planned for high-risk disease.
An open approach is favoured for non-organ-confined disease; if a minimally invasive approach is used, follow measures intended to prevent tumour spillage.
Discuss patients with suspected UTUC on imaging in a multidisciplinary team before treatment begins.

recommended_regimens.name: Radical nephroureterectomy
recommended_regimens.summary: Standard surgery for high-risk non-metastatic UTUC; remove the kidney and ureter en bloc with the bladder cuff according to oncological principles.

recommended_regimens.name: Template-based lymphadenectomy
recommended_regimens.summary: Offer alongside RNU for high-risk non-metastatic disease. LND improves staging; the guideline's evidence summary reports improved survival in muscle-invasive UTUC.

alternative_regimens.name: Laparoscopic RNU
alternative_regimens.summary: An experienced team may use a minimally invasive approach while adhering to strict oncological principles; approaches have similar oncological outcomes for organ-confined UTUC.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Organ-confined disease and capacity to prevent tumour spillage. A small randomised trial (n = 80) found inferior outcomes relative to open RNU in non-organ-confined disease.

alternative_regimens.name: Robot-assisted laparoscopic approach
alternative_regimens.summary: May be considered, with peri-operative benefits comparable to standard laparoscopy and data suggesting oncological equivalence for organ-confined disease.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Selected patients in whom a minimally invasive approach is appropriate.

response_assessment.method: Pathological assessment of pT stage, nodal status and surgical margins
response_assessment.interpretation: Findings guide eligibility for adjuvant treatment and subsequent surveillance.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Open RNU for non-organ-confined UTUC has a separate Weak recommendation. For minimally invasive surgery, avoid tumour contact and morcellation, use a closed system and an endobag, and avoid opening the urinary tract except during bladder cuff excision after ureteral clipping and bladder drainage. Intravesical recurrence may be more frequent after laparoscopic or robotic RNU than after open surgery. Complete bladder cuff removal matters because incomplete excision increases BC recurrence.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Highly selected patients whose high-risk tumour is confined to the distal ureter.
decision_rules: Offer distal ureterectomy only in selected patients when its potential benefits outweigh its risks.
Concomitant lymph node dissection may be performed.

recommended_regimens.name: Distal ureterectomy
recommended_regimens.summary: An organ-preserving option for selected high-risk tumours limited to the distal ureter.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: Available evidence suggests oncological outcomes similar to RNU for high-risk disease limited to the distal ureter, but the evidence level is low.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The guideline limits this approach to highly selected cases because supporting evidence is weak.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with an imperative reason to avoid RNU, such as a solitary kidney, bilateral UTUC, severe chronic kidney disease or another comorbidity that compromises RNU.
decision_rules: Discuss kidney-sparing treatment individually through shared decision-making despite its higher progression risk.
Select ureteroscopy or segmental ureterectomy according to the case.

recommended_regimens.name: Kidney-sparing management
recommended_regimens.summary: A case-by-case option to discuss when an imperative indication makes RNU problematic; possible procedures include ureteroscopy and segmental ureterectomy.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: Progression is more likely after kidney-sparing surgery for high-risk than for low-risk UTUC, with a direct effect on survival.

response_assessment.interpretation: If no residual tumour is found, use follow-up principles similar to those for high-risk disease treated with RNU.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The ipsilateral upper tract needs careful long-term surveillance because recurrence risk remains high.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients considered for neoadjuvant treatment before RNU, particularly those with high-grade and/or cT2-T4N0M0 UTUC while renal function still permits cisplatin.
decision_rules: Cisplatin-based NAC may be considered before RNU to use the renal function available before kidney removal.
Interpret apparent survival benefits cautiously because randomised evidence is lacking and the cited meta-analysis has substantial bias and heterogeneity.

alternative_regimens.name: cisplatin combination therapy
alternative_regimens.summary: Prospective phase II trials reported a 14 - 19% pathological complete response rate in high-grade and/or cT2-T4N0M0 UTUC; final pathological stage was < ypT1 in more than 60% of included patients. A systematic review and meta-analysis of more than 800 patients reported pathological partial response of 43% and downstaging in 33%, with an OS and CSS benefit versus RNU alone; those findings were not conclusive.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Potential neoadjuvant option while renal function allows cisplatin; the guideline does not provide a formal recommendation grade for NAC.

not_recommended.name: Carboplatin
not_recommended.reason: The guideline states that Carboplatin is not indicated for neoadjuvant treatment.

not_recommended.name: Neoadjuvant immunotherapy
not_recommended.reason: Evidence does not currently support its use for high-risk UTUC. A small phase II pembrolizumab study in 10 patients observed no pathological response and reported one treatment-related death.

response_assessment.interpretation: Assess complete response and downstaging; the guideline associates pathological downstaging after neoadjuvant treatment with better OS.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The cited meta-analysis did not clearly separate truly neoadjuvant from downstaging chemotherapy.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Eligible patients after RNU with pT2–T4 and/or pN+ disease.
decision_rules: Offer adjuvant platinum-based chemotherapy after RNU to eligible patients.
Determine cisplatin or carboplatin eligibility from renal function and the other criteria in the guideline's platinum-eligibility table.
Consider that renal function may worsen after RNU and prevent cisplatin treatment.

recommended_regimens.name: gemcitabine/cisplatin
recommended_regimens.summary: An adjuvant platinum-based option for eligible patients after RNU. In the phase III trial, patients were assigned cisplatin or carboplatin with gemcitabine according to GFR, with benefit regardless of platinum type.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: For the trial's adjuvant gemcitabine-platinum chemotherapy versus surveillance comparison: 3 year DFS 71% vs 50%; 5 year DFS 63% vs 46%; HR 0.54 ; CI 0.36-0.79; 3 & 5 year MFS 19 % improvement HR 0.55 CI 0.0.36-0.77. The OS trend was non-significant (12% at 3 years). These outcomes were reported for the combined platinum-treatment population, not separately for gemcitabine/cisplatin.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: four cycles, initiated within 90 days after RNU

recommended_regimens.name: gemcitabine/ carboplatin
recommended_regimens.summary: An adjuvant platinum-based option when GFR determines use of carboplatin rather than cisplatin. The phase III trial reported benefit irrespective of platinum type.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The phase III trial reported, for its combined gemcitabine-platinum population versus surveillance, 3 year DFS 71% vs 50%; 5 year DFS 63% vs 46%; HR 0.54 ; CI 0.36-0.79; 3 & 5 year MFS 19 % improvement HR 0.55 CI 0.0.36-0.77. These are not separate gemcitabine/ carboplatin outcomes.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: four cycles, initiated within 90 days after RNU

response_assessment.interpretation: Identify patients with pT2–T4 and/or pN+ disease for adjuvant treatment.

supportive_care: With split dose and hydration, cisplatin may be considered when GFR is down to 45 mL/min.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The trial closed after reaching its DFS endpoint and was underpowered for OS. Consider adjuvant chemotherapy when UC is the dominant pathology despite retrospective evidence of differing outcomes among histological subtypes.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients after RNU without a history of BC.
decision_rules: Give one post-operative intravesical chemotherapy instillation to reduce bladder recurrence.
If drug extravasation is a concern, consider a cystogram before instillation.

recommended_regimens.name: mitomycin C
recommended_regimens.summary: One post-operative intravesical chemotherapy option supported by trials and meta-analyses in patients without prior BC.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: Trials and meta-analyses found reduced bladder tumour recurrence during the first years after RNU; the reported bladder recurrence rate after RNU for UTUC is 22–47%.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: A single dose 2–10 days after surgery

recommended_regimens.name: pirarubicin
recommended_regimens.summary: One post-operative intravesical chemotherapy option supported by trials and meta-analyses in patients without prior BC.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: Trials and meta-analyses found reduced bladder tumour recurrence during the first years after RNU; the reported bladder recurrence rate after RNU for UTUC is 22–47%.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: A single dose 2–10 days after surgery

supportive_care: Consider a cystogram before instillation if extravasation is suspected.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Intravesical treatment has also been given at RNU before opening the bladder cuff, with limited efficacy data. Additional instillations beyond one peri-operative dose are unlikely to substantially reduce recurrence further.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients unfit for, or declining, platinum-based adjuvant chemotherapy who have > pT3 and/or pN+ disease after RNU alone, or > ypT2 and/or ypN+ disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by RNU.
treatment_pathways.biomarker_condition: The EMA-approved adjuvant indication described in the guideline requires tumour cell PD-L1 expression > 1%.
decision_rules: Discuss adjuvant nivolumab with patients meeting the specified post-operative criteria who cannot or do not wish to receive platinum-based adjuvant chemotherapy.
Explain that the UTUC subgroup of the cited trial did not appear to benefit and requires further follow-up and analysis.

recommended_regimens.name: nivolumab
recommended_regimens.summary: An adjuvant treatment to discuss, rather than an established UTUC-specific benefit, for the specified patients after RNU.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In the predominantly BC phase III trial, DFS was 20.8 vs. 10.8 months for nivolumab versus placebo in the intention-to-treat population; the UTUC subgroup did not appear to benefit. Treatment-related adverse events > grade 3 occurred in 17.9% of the nivolumab group and 7.2% of the placebo group.

response_assessment.timepoint: After RNU, with or without previous neoadjuvant chemotherapy
response_assessment.method: Pathological pT or ypT and nodal staging
response_assessment.interpretation: Apply the respective > pT3 and/or pN+ or > ypT2 and/or ypN+ criteria.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The EMA approval discussed in the guideline applies to high-risk muscle-invasive UC after radical surgery with tumour cell PD-L1 expression > 1% when adjuvant chemotherapy is declined or unsuitable. A network meta-analysis suggests greater oncological benefit from adjuvant platinum chemotherapy than from immune checkpoint inhibitors after surgery for UTUC.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with clinically N+ UTUC.
decision_rules: Offer first-line platinum-based chemotherapy for downstaging.
If disease responds or remains stable, maintenance avelumab can be offered, particularly for cN2 disease.
After a response to initial systemic treatment, discuss resection with LN dissection according to cN1/N2 disease extent in a multidisciplinary team and with the patient.
If disease progresses, consider treatment as for metastatic disease.

recommended_regimens.name: platinum-based chemotherapy
recommended_regimens.summary: Initial systemic treatment offered to downstage clinically node-positive UTUC.

alternative_regimens.name: Surgical resection with LN dissection
alternative_regimens.summary: A possible local treatment after initial systemic therapy.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Discuss after a response, considering nodal extent and the multidisciplinary and patient discussions.

response_assessment.method: Assessment of response, stable disease or progression
response_assessment.interpretation: Response may lead to discussion of surgery; response or stability may permit maintenance avelumab; progression directs consideration of later-line metastatic treatment.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The guideline states that evidence is lacking on the optimal management of clinically node-positive disease.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with advanced or metastatic disease who can receive combination therapy.
decision_rules: Offer enfortumab vedotin together with pembrolizumab as first-line treatment.
If the combination is unsuitable, unavailable or contraindicated, select a platinum-based or other eligible first-line pathway.

recommended_regimens.name: Enfortumab vedotin + pembrolizumab
recommended_regimens.summary: Preferred first-line combination for advanced or metastatic disease. The cited EV302 phase III study compared the combination with platinum-based combination chemotherapy.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: EV302 reported PFS HR 0.45 (0.38-0.54 ) and OS HR 0.47 (0.38-0.58); RR was 68% (versus 44%) and CR was 29%. The proportion of UTUC patients in this study was not yet known.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: EV302 reported grade 3 or above treatment-related skin reactions (15.5%), peripheral neuropathy (6.8%) and hyperglycaemia (6.1%). Treatment sequencing after this combination remains unclear and depends on earlier agents received.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with advanced or metastatic disease unsuitable for Enfortumab + Pembrolizumab who are eligible for cisplatin-based combination chemotherapy.
decision_rules: Offer platinum combination chemotherapy; cisplatin-containing combinations are standard treatment in this population.
Offer gemcitabine/cisplatin or HD-MVAC to cisplatin-eligible patients.
Gemcitabine-cisplatin plus nivolumab may also be offered, with a Weak recommendation.

recommended_regimens.name: gemcitabine/cisplatin
recommended_regimens.summary: A widely used cisplatin-containing first-line combination for eligible patients unable to receive Enfortumab + Pembrolizumab.

recommended_regimens.name: HD-MVAC
recommended_regimens.summary: A cisplatin-containing first-line chemotherapy option for eligible patients unable to receive Enfortumab + Pembrolizumab.

recommended_regimens.name: gemcitabine-cisplatin + nivolumab
recommended_regimens.summary: A first-line combination that may be offered to cisplatin-eligible patients. The cited phase III study did not provide an analysis by primary tumour site; 12.6% of its participants had UTUC.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In the advanced/metastatic UC trial, median OS was 21.7 months v 18.9 months, HR 0.78 (0.63-0.96); median PFS was 7.9 months versus 7.6 months, HR 0.72 (0.59-0.88); objective RR was 57.6% compared with 43.1 % for chemotherapy alone.

response_assessment.timepoint: After 4–6 cycles of first-line platinum-based chemotherapy
response_assessment.method: Assessment for complete response, partial response, stable disease or progression
response_assessment.interpretation: Patients without progression may proceed to first-line maintenance avelumab.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The guideline states that cisplatin-based chemotherapy is widely considered at eGFR > 45 mL/min, while its platinum-eligibility table specifies ECOG PS 0-1, GFR > 50–60 mL/min and additional hearing, neuropathy and cardiac criteria. The first-line nivolumab combination trial did not report a UTUC-specific efficacy subgroup.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients unsuitable for Enfortumab + Pembrolizumab and unfit for cisplatin but eligible for carboplatin-based combination chemotherapy.
treatment_pathways.biomarker_condition: Choice of gemcitabine/carboplatin is irrespective of PDL-1 status.
decision_rules: Offer gemcitabine/carboplatin to cisplatin-ineligible patients.

recommended_regimens.name: gemcitabine/carboplatin
recommended_regimens.summary: Preferred carboplatin-based first-line combination for patients unable to receive cisplatin.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The guideline's evidence summary states that carboplatin-based combination chemotherapy provides a survival benefit in patients unfit for cisplatin.

response_assessment.timepoint: After 4–6 cycles of first-line platinum-based chemotherapy
response_assessment.method: Assessment for complete response, partial response, stable disease or progression
response_assessment.interpretation: Disease that has not progressed may qualify for maintenance avelumab.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The guideline's platinum-eligibility table describes carboplatin eligibility as ECOG PS 2 or GFR 30–60 mL/ min or failure to meet another cisplatin-eligibility criterion; it separately lists circumstances that make a patient platinum-ineligible.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with complete or partial response or stable disease, without progression, after first-line platinum-based combination chemotherapy.
decision_rules: Offer avelumab as maintenance only after non-progressive disease following first-line platinum-based combination chemotherapy.
Do not extend the maintenance avelumab evidence to platinum chemotherapy delivered outside the first-line setting.

recommended_regimens.name: avelumab
recommended_regimens.summary: Maintenance following first-line gemcitabine with cisplatin or carboplatin in advanced or metastatic disease that has not progressed.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The cited phase III trial reported OS HR: 0.69; 95% CI: 0.56–0.86 versus best supportive care alone, with median OS increasing from 14 to 21 months. Almost 30% of participants had UTUC, but no tumour-location subgroup analysis was available.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: Start within 10 weeks after completing 4 to 6 cycles of first-line platinum-based chemotherapy.

not_recommended.name: Maintenance avelumab outside the first-line setting
not_recommended.reason: The guideline states that no data support this use.

response_assessment.timepoint: After 4–6 cycles of first-line platinum-based chemotherapy
response_assessment.method: Assessment for complete response, partial response, stable disease or progression
response_assessment.interpretation: Only patients without progression enter the maintenance pathway.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: A separate phase II study reported improved PFS with maintenance pembrolizumab versus placebo (5.4 vs. 3.0 months) in metastatic UC after at least stable disease on first-line platinum chemotherapy; the formal maintenance recommendation in this guideline is for avelumab.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients ineligible for any combination therapy, including those unfit for platinum-based chemotherapy.
decision_rules: Offer pembrolizumab or atezolizumab as single-agent checkpoint inhibition only to patients with PD-L1 positive tumours in this pathway.

recommended_regimens.name: pembrolizumab
recommended_regimens.summary: A first-line checkpoint inhibitor option for PD-L1 positive patients who cannot receive combination therapy.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In a single-arm phase II trial of cisplatin-ineligible UC, the objective response rate was 26% among 69 metastatic UTUC patients; the overall study enrolled n = 370. In the overall cohort, PD-L1 expression of 10% was associated with a greater response rate.

recommended_regimens.name: atezolizumab
recommended_regimens.summary: A first-line checkpoint inhibitor option for PD-L1 positive patients who cannot receive combination therapy.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In a single-arm phase II trial of cisplatin-ineligible UC, the objective response rate was 39% among 33 (28%) metastatic UTUC patients; the study enrolled n = 119. Median OS of 15.9 months refers to the overall cohort, not specifically to UTUC.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The guideline restricts these first-line monotherapy options to PD-L1 positive disease. Treatment-related toxicity in the cited studies was reported as consistent with previous studies.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients requiring second-line systemic treatment who did not receive platinum-based combination chemotherapy first line.
decision_rules: Offer platinum-based combination chemotherapy as the second-line treatment of choice if it was not given first line.
Select the platinum agent according to the patient's eligibility.

recommended_regimens.name: platinum based combination chemotherapy
recommended_regimens.summary: The preferred second-line treatment when platinum combination chemotherapy was not previously administered.

not_recommended.name: Maintenance avelumab after second-line platinum chemotherapy
not_recommended.reason: No data support maintenance avelumab outside the first-line setting.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Later-line selection depends on which agents the patient received earlier.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients whose metastatic disease progresses during or after platinum-based combination chemotherapy and who did not receive maintenance avelumab.
decision_rules: Offer pembrolizumab after progression on platinum-based combination chemotherapy if maintenance avelumab was not received.

recommended_regimens.name: pembrolizumab
recommended_regimens.summary: Checkpoint inhibitor treatment following progression during or after platinum-based combination chemotherapy in patients without prior maintenance avelumab.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In the cited phase III advanced-UC trial, median OS was 10.3 months with pembrolizumab versus 7.4 months with investigator-selected chemotherapy (HR: 0.73; 95% CI: 0.59–0.91), and responses occurred in 21% vs. 11%. In the UTUC subgroup (n = 75/13.8%), the OS benefit appeared larger (50%).

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The phase III comparator was the investigator's choice of paclitaxel, docetaxel or vinflunine. A separate atezolizumab trial in PD-L1-positive disease did not show a significant OS advantage over second-line chemotherapy.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients previously treated with platinum-containing chemotherapy whose disease progressed during or after PD-1 or PD-L1 inhibitor treatment.
decision_rules: Offer enfortumab vedotin when both prior platinum exposure and progression during or after PD-1 or PD-L1 treatment are present.

recommended_regimens.name: enfortumab vedotin
recommended_regimens.summary: Subsequent-line antibody–drug conjugate for disease progressing after the specified prior treatments.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: A phase III trial reported median OS of 12.88 vs. 8.97 months for enfortumab vedotin versus standard chemotherapy. A separate phase II study of 89 cisplatin-unfit patients after PD-1 or PD-L1 therapy, of whom 43% had UTUC, reported a 52% objective radiological response rate and 20% complete responses.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Earlier treatment determines later-line sequencing; the guideline notes particular uncertainty after first-line Enfortumab vedotin + pembrolizumab.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients previously treated with platinum-containing chemotherapy whose disease progressed during or after PD-1 or PD-L1 inhibitor treatment.
treatment_pathways.biomarker_condition: FGFR DNA genomic alterations (FGFR2/3 mutations or FGFR3 fusions)
decision_rules: Test for FGFR alterations before erdafitinib.
Offer erdafitinib as an alternative subsequent-line therapy only when the specified FGFR alteration and prior-treatment conditions are met.

alternative_regimens.name: erdafitinib
alternative_regimens.summary: A Strong-graded alternative subsequent-line treatment for patients meeting the molecular and prior-treatment criteria. In the phase II study, radiological response was 40% across 99 advanced-UC patients and 43% among the 23 included UTUC patients with visceral metastases. The phase III Thor trial reported a median OS improvement of 4.3 months (HR 0.64;CI 0.47-0.88), a PFS improvement of 2.9 months (58; CI 0.44-0.78) and a 36% reduction in risk of death; 33.5 % of participants had UTUC.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Prior platinum-containing chemotherapy, progression during or after PD-1 or PD-L1 inhibitor treatment, and FGFR DNA genomic alterations (FGFR2/3 mutations or FGFR3 fusions).
